nodes.name: Daily
nodes.notes: One video a day at 09:00 local. The arc is finite: when --series runs out of parts the Render node fails on purpose and this trigger keeps firing, so a run that fails with "Every episode ... has been published" means write the next part, not fix the workflow.

nodes.name: Render
nodes.notes: --series renders the next unpublished part of the arc, chosen by history.json, so the schedule needs no counter of its own. The node has no working-directory setting, so the cd is part of the command. The 8.3 short path is deliberate: cmd.exe cannot read the accented characters in the real path. --stage drops a copy of the video and cover in C:\n8n-data under fixed names, which is the only place n8n is allowed to read files from. Call node directly, not npm: npm prints its own banner to stdout and would break the JSON contract.

nodes.name: Read the video
nodes.notes: Read/Write Files from Disk, not the older Read Binary File: that node is deprecated and fails on current n8n with 'The file has changed and cannot be accessed'.

YouTube requires realistic synthetic content to be disclosed, and the YouTube node cannot: containsSyntheticMedia appears nowhere in it, so this sets it through the API afterwards. videos.update replaces the whole part it is given, so privacyStatus and selfDeclaredMadeForKids are repeated here on purpose — omitting privacyStatus would clear it and take the video out of private. part=status leaves the snippet alone, so the title, description and tags are not at risk.
nodes.name: Say it is synthetic
Read the cover
nodes.notes: A run with --no-cover stages no cover. Disable this node and the one after it if you turn covers off.

videoId comes from uploadId, not id. The YouTube node uploads in resumable chunks and returns { uploadId, ...initiateResponse.body }; the initiate call has an empty body, so there is no id field. Reading .id sends videoId=undefined, and the HTTP Request node hides Google refusal behind a circular-structure error.
